question.leadin: One of these people named Harald Hardrada lost at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.
question.text: Name these warrior seafarers that ravaged the coasts of Great Britain in the late first millennium. They hailed from Scandinavia and had kings such as Cnut (k'NOOT) and Sven Forkbeard.
question.clue: The life and voyages of these people are told in works known as sagas.

swap.leadin: This country joined the European Union in 1995, and opened the Oresund Bridge in 2000, which connected its city of Malmo to Denmark.
swap.text: Name this country, whose Prime Minister Olof Palme was assassinated in 1986 while walking from a movie with his wife. Ingvar Carlsson succeeded Palme as Prime Minister of this country.
swap.clue: The Ottoman Sultan Ahmed III gave refuge to this country's monarch and the cossack Ivan Mazeppa after his forces lost the Battle of Poltava.

question.leadin: Leather cannons used by this man's army allowed his artillery unprecedented mobility in combat.
question.text: Name this Swedish ruler nicknamed "The Lion of the North," who was advised by Axel Oxenstierna and transformed Sweden into a leading European power.
question.clue: This ruler's chancellor, Axel Oxenstierna, continued to fight the war in which this ruler died while fighting Wallenstein at the Battle of Lutzen.

swap.leadin: Axel Oxenstierna advised this son of Charles IX, who soundly defeated the Count of Tilly at Breitenfeld in 1631.
swap.text: Name this ruler, who later led a victory over the Holy Roman Empire at Lutzen but was killed in the process.
swap.answerHtml: Gustavus Adolphus (or Gustav II Adolf; prompt on partial answer)
swap.clue: In addition to ending the Kalmar War, one military rival to this person employed an elector named Maximilian I that died with him at Ingolstadt after losing to the numerically superior force of this ruler at the Battle of the Rain.

question.leadin: The Treaty of Knared ended a war that shares a name with this union.
question.text: Name this union of Scandinavia first ruled by Eric of Pomerania to counter the influence of the Hanseatic League.
question.clue: This polity was weakened by earlier rebellions led by Amund Bolt in one member and Engelbrekt in another, leading to the deposition of its monarch, Eric of Pomerania.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about people whose names have become synonymous with the word traitor.
swap.text: This man collaborated with the Germans after the invasion of his country, and requested to be made the 'Fuhrer of Norway'. He was found guilty of high treason by the allies and sentenced to death after the war.
swap.clue: This politician launched their political career in a series of articles explaining their 'political thoughts' on the death of mentor Fritjohf Nansen.
swap.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

question.leadin: This god transformed into a snake to retrieve the divine mead of inspiration.
question.text: Name this chief god of the Norse myth system. He has one eye and is advised by the ravens Hunin and Mugin.

swap.text: The Hanse became involved in political issues as well, such as the Swedish War of Liberation, in which Gustav Vasa deposed a Norwegian-Danish king of this name as regent of the Kalmar Union. That "second" king of this name had carried out the Stockholm Bloodbath.
swap.clue: After the Englebrecht Rebellion, the Swedish gained some independence before this ruler's invasion in 1520. An ally of Gustav Trolle, he perpetrated the Stockholm Bloodbath. In karmic retaliation, Frederick I imprisoned this man for 27 years.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Polish Golden Age history.
question.text: The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was ruled by Wladyslaw [vwah-DIS-waf] IV, a member of this royal house. A ship named after this house sank after only traveling 1,400 yards, and its member Sigismund III was overthrown by Charles IX.
question.clue: A queen from this royal house abdicated after converting to Catholicism and housed Descartes in his final years.

swap.text: In the 1920s, the League of Nations notably arbitrated Finland's dispute with Sweden over these islands in the mouth of the Gulf of Bothnia. The League found them to be over 90% Swedish in population, and thus naturally awarded them to Finland.
swap.clue: This archipelago in the Baltic Sea that was the subject of a dispute between Sweden and Finland that ended with these islands of Swedes staying Finnish but becoming mostly autonomous.

question.leadin: The Archipelago Ring Road connects the cities in this country's Archipelago Sea.
question.text: Name this Scandinavian country that contains the region of North Karelia and the Swedish-speaking Aland Islands, and which has its capital on the shore of a namesake gulf.
question.clue: As a grand duchy, this country's capital was originally at Turku.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of some islands in Europe that are not Great Britain or Ireland.
swap.text: This Norwegian territory's namesake treaty regulates commercial and military activities. This Arctic archipelago is home to one of the largest seed banks in the world -- the Global Seed Vault.
swap.answerHtml: Svalbard [prompt on Spitsbergen; do NOT accept or prompt on “Jan Mayen”]
swap.clue: The name of this Norwegian archipelago means "cold shores," and its three inhabited islands are Spitzbergen, Bear Island, and Hopen.

question.text: Women's suffrage was signed into law by the king of this country, which owned Iceland at the time and still owns Greenland.
question.clue: This country was defeated in one war after its adversary marched over a frozen strait to surprise its forces.

swap.leadin: A company from this country manufactured a 40 millimeter cannon that became one of the most popular anti-aircraft guns on both sides in World War II.
swap.text: Name this country home to Bofors ["BOH-furs"] whose defense industry also includes the builder of the Gripen jet fighter, Saab.
swap.clue: Gutnish is spoken on this country's largest island.

question.text: Hone Heke cut down James Busby's flagstaff to start the First Maori War, which is often described with this term. It is also applied to a "Great" conflict fought between Charles XII and Peter the Great.
question.clue: The second conflict of this name saw Azov returned to the Ottoman Turks following their victory at the Battle of Pruth River.

swap.text: Quisling had previously worked with this man organizing relief for the 1921 Russian famine. This man won a Nobel Peace Prize partly for developing a type of passport for stateless refugees.
swap.clue: He prodded the British navy and directed the Red Cross in overseeing the repatriation of over 400,000 Soviet prisoners of war, which earned him the Nobel Peace Prize.

question.text: Jon remained loyal to this city's exiled archbishop Olav Engelbrektsson, who led the Norwegian Riksrad ("reeks-ROAD") until its 1537 dissolution with the Reformation. Pilgrims visited Saint Olaf's shrine at this city's cathedral.
question.clue: This city founded in 997 by Olaf Tryggvason, the medieval capital of Norway.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Norway's civil war era.
swap.text: The civil war developed into a war between the aristocratic Bagler faction and a rebellious commoner faction named for this material. The faction got its name because its members were supposedly so poor that they made their shoes from this material.
swap.answerHtml: birchbark [accept Birkebeiner, Birkebeinar, Birkebein Party, or Birkebein faction; prompt on wood or bark]

question.text: Upon his 1946 death, Hansson was succeeded by this prime minister, Sweden's longest serving. This man continued Hansson's folkhemmet, and made the Swedish Air Force the third largest in the world.

swap.text: The Age of Liberty was ended by this king, who seized power from the parliament in 1777. Ruling as an enlightened despot, he established freedom of the press and religious toleration before being assassinated by dissident nobles in 1792.
swap.clue: This enlightened despot who ended his country's Age of Liberty with the Union and Security Act. This ruler signed the Treaty of Varala to end a war with Catherine the Great.
